reason: Each normative requirement maps to an assertion that fails when it is violated. (1) Scope hierarchy read<write<admin: test_fr04_scope_hierarchy_matrix asserts read→403 and write→201 on POST at lines 102-103, and read/write→403 with admin→204 on DELETE at lines 105-107. test_fr04_write_key_can_read asserts write→200 on GET at line 115. (2) Insufficient scope returns 403 with problem+json: lines 124-127 assert the status, the application/problem+json content type and the /errors/forbidden type. (3) The body must not reveal whether the resource exists: test_fr04_403_does_not_leak_existence compares an existing id with a random unknown id under a write key on DELETE (admin required). Lines 147-153 assert equal status, type and detail, and that neither id appears in the body. test_sec_t03 asserts the same at lines 208-212. (4) Single dependency: line 181 walks every /v1 APIRoute's dependant tree and fails if any route lacks the require_scope closure from deps. Line 179 guards against an empty route list. The expected values come from the spec (403, 0 unguarded), not from the implementation. Minor limit: the dependency test shows each route is guarded, not that its minimum scope matches the FR-01/02 table. The matrix covers that only for POST and DELETE /v1/tasks.

gaps.message: The route-dependency test confirms every /v1 route includes a require_scope dependency but does not assert the per-route minimum scope. GET /v1/tasks/{id}, GET /v1/tasks/{id}/runs, POST /v1/tasks/{id}/run and /v1/metrics are only covered indirectly. This is not a requirement violation.
